text: Two studies illuminate bacterial two-component signalling. A 1.40 Å crystal structure of the CheA3 phosphotransfer domain bound to its cognate response regulator CheY6 revealed a methionine finger inserting into a hydrophobic pocket in CheA3; this residue occurs only in cognate CheY6 and CheB2. Mutating it plus two adjacent residues abolished binding (surface plasmon resonance) and phosphotransfer, whereas introducing methionine and an adjacent alanine into noncognate CheYs reengineered their specificity, enabling rapid phosphotransfer from CheA3-P. Separately, in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the ppk1 promoter is activated by phosphate starvation: deletion of an imperfect palindrome (a phosphorylated RegX3 binding site, confirmed by electrophoretic mobility shift assay) attenuated it, deletion of a SigE site abrogated it, SigE binding was confirmed by pull-down and in vitro transcription, and RseA overexpression reduced ppk1 expression.
